html:
A bombing at a labour rally in Chicago on 4 May 1886, and the trial that followed. It is the reason much of the world marks May Day as a workers' holiday.

On 1 May 1886 hundreds of thousands of American workers struck for the eight-hour day. On 3 May police shot and killed strikers outside the McCormick reaper works. Anarchists called a protest meeting the next evening in Haymarket Square. It was peaceful until police moved in to break it up. Then someone threw a bomb. Police opened fire. Seven police officers and at least four civilians died.

No one ever proved who threw the bomb. Eight anarchists were convicted anyway, mostly for their speeches and writings. Four were hanged in 1887 and one killed himself in prison. In 1893 the governor of Illinois pardoned the three still alive and condemned the trial as unjust.

In 1889 the socialist Second International chose 1 May as International Workers' Day in their memory. The United States itself keeps Labor Day in September instead.
sum: A bombing at a labour rally in Chicago on 4 May 1886, and the trial that followed. It is the reason much of the world marks May Day as a workers' holiday.
